// A fixture of code the check must be SILENT on (RL-M2-006).
//
// The half that keeps the check usable. A rule that fires on everything is as useless as one
// that fires on nothing, and it is the version that gets disabled rather than fixed — so
// every legitimate shape the agent and privd actually need is here.
package fixture

import (
	"context"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"os"
)

// The agent's own work: dialling out. Nothing in here listens.
func dialOut(ctx context.Context) {
	client := &http.Client{}
	request, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, "https://control/agent/challenge", nil)
	client.Do(request)

	var dialer net.Dialer
	dialer.DialContext(ctx, "tcp", "control.example:443")
	net.Dial("tcp", "control.example:443")
}

// privd's socket (ADR 0004). A unix-domain socket is not a port: it lives in the filesystem,
// it is protected by peer credentials and file mode, and nothing off the host can reach it.
// A check that refused this could not tell "the fleet exposes nothing new" from "the two
// components on a host cannot talk".
func privdSocket() {
	net.Listen("unix", "/run/ratline/privd.sock")
	net.ListenUnix("unix", nil)
	net.ListenPacket("unixgram", "/run/ratline/privd.dgram")
}

// Socket activation, with the reason written down. systemd may hand privd its listening
// socket on fd 3 rather than having privd bind it, which is the shape ADR 0004 describes and
// which no literal in the source can classify.
//
// The reason WRAPS on purpose. shellcheck's version of this annotation permits its own line
// and the next one, which silently stops applying when the text runs to two lines — a build
// failure about an unclassified listener sitting directly beneath a comment classifying it.
// Here the permitted line is the one after the whole comment group.
func socketActivation() {
	var file *os.File
	//ratline:allow-listener systemd passes privd a unix socket on fd 3; the unit declares
	// ListenStream= with a filesystem path, so no port is involved (ADR 0004)
	net.FileListener(file)
}

// The trailing spelling, which reads better on a short call.
func socketActivationBeside() {
	var file *os.File
	net.FileListener(file) //ratline:allow-listener the same fd 3 unix socket, stated beside it
}

// Words that are not calls. A grep over this file would fire several times: Listen,
// ListenAndServe, net.Listen("tcp", …) inside a sentence explaining why the agent does not
// do that. go/ast never visits a comment as an expression, which is the whole reason this
// check is a walk and not a grep — the TypeScript side learned it four separate times
// (RL-M1-041).
func prose() {
	// The strings below are data, not calls. A configuration file naming a port, or an error
	// message about one, must not trip the check.
	_ = "tcp"
	_ = []string{"tcp", "udp", "ListenAndServe"}
}
